title: Indirect object pronouns: le, les, se
summary: To whom and for whom: le regalo flores a mi madre, se lo doy, nos faltan dos euros.
focus: Indirect object pronouns me, te, le, nos, os, les; se lo; the redundant a él / a ella; gustar-type verbs
content:
## The indirect object: to whom, for whom

The **indirect object** is the person who receives the thing or benefits from the action. Ask *¿a quién?* after the verb and its object:

- *Doy el libro a Marta.* (¿A quién doy el libro? A Marta.)

The pronouns:

| | singular | plural |
|---|---|---|
| 1st person | **me** (to me) | **nos** (to us) |
| 2nd person | **te** (to you) | **os** (to you all) |
| 3rd person | **le** (to him, to her, to you *usted*) | **les** (to them, to you all) |

Only **le / les** differ from the direct object pronouns, and they have **no gender**. Examples:

- *Le regalo flores.* (I give him/her flowers.)
- *Te escribo un correo.* (I'll write you an email.)
- *Nos explica la gramática.* (She explains the grammar to us.)

## Say it twice: a él, a ella, a mi madre

Because *le* can mean him, her or you, Spanish usually keeps the pronoun **and** names the person. This "double" is normal and correct:

- *Le regalo flores a mi madre.* (I give my mother flowers.)
- *Les envío una foto a mis padres.* (I send my parents a photo.)
- *¿A usted le interesa el arte?* (Are you interested in art?)

The same **a + pronoun** adds emphasis or contrast: *A mí me gusta el café, pero a él le gusta el té.* The forms are **a mí**, **a ti**, **a él / a ella / a usted**, **a nosotros**, **a vosotros**, **a ellos / a ellas / a ustedes**.

## Two pronouns: indirect first, then le becomes se

When a sentence has both pronouns, the **indirect comes first**, then the direct:

- *¿El libro? Me lo das mañana.* (You'll give it to me tomorrow.)
- *¿Tu móvil? Te lo presto.* (I'll lend it to you.)

**Le / les** cannot stand next to *lo, la, los, las*: they change to **se**.

- *Le doy el libro a Juan.* → *Se lo doy.* (I give it to him.)
- *Les envío las fotos.* → *Se las envío.* (I send them to them.)

Position is the same as for direct objects. The pronouns go before the conjugated verb, or attach to an infinitive or gerund (with an accent): *Quiero dártelo* = *Te lo quiero dar*.

## Gustar's family

Several common verbs work like **gustar**. The person is an indirect object, and the verb agrees with the **thing**:

| verb | example |
|---|---|
| encantar | *Me encanta el chocolate.* (I love chocolate.) |
| interesar | *¿Te interesa la historia?* (Are you interested in history?) |
| parecer | *¿Qué os parece el plan?* (What do you think of the plan?) |
| doler | *Le duele la cabeza. Le duelen los pies.* (Her head hurts. Her feet hurt.) |
| faltar | *Nos faltan dos euros.* (We are two euros short.) |
| quedar | *Me quedan tres días de vacaciones.* (I have three days of holiday left.) |

A singular thing takes a singular verb (*falta*, *queda*). A plural thing takes a plural verb (*faltan*, *quedan*).

quiz.explanation: Mi madre receives the flowers, so she is the indirect object and the pronoun is 'le'. The direct object is 'flores'. Indirect pronouns have no gender.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the pronoun meaning 'to me': ¿___ prestas tu móvil?
quiz.explanation: 'To me' is 'me', placed in front of the conjugated verb: '¿Me prestas tu móvil?'

quiz.prompt: ___ envío una foto a mis padres.
quiz.explanation: Mis padres are plural recipients, so the pronoun is 'les'. 'Los' would make them the direct object, but the photo is what gets sent.
hints: They receive the photo; they are not sent.

quiz.prompt: Replace both objects: Le pido un favor a mi hermano. → ___ lo pido.
quiz.explanation: Before lo, la, los or las, le turns into se: 'Se lo pido.'
hints: Le changes into a two-letter word.

quiz.explanation: 'Te' is the indirect object (to you). The book is the direct object, masculine singular, so it is 'lo': 'Te lo devuelvo.'
The indirect pronoun (nos) comes before the direct pronoun (lo): 'Nos lo explica.'

quiz.prompt: Complete with the correct form of parecer: ¿Qué te ___ la película?
quiz.explanation: Parecer works like gustar: the verb agrees with the thing (la película, singular): '¿Qué te parece la película?'

quiz.prompt: A mis padres ___ interesa mucho la historia.
quiz.explanation: Even when the people are named ('a mis padres'), the pronoun stays, and it is plural: 'les'.
hints: Naming the person does not remove the pronoun.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the correct form of faltar: Nos ___ dos euros.
quiz.explanation: The verb agrees with what is missing (dos euros, plural): 'Nos faltan dos euros.' We are the indirect object.

guide.tip: Not sure if it's lo or le? Ask what gets handed over. The thing handed over is lo/la, and the person who gets it is le.

conversations.title: A present for mum
conversations.scenario: Elena and her brother Raúl are planning their mother's birthday present.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Raúl, ¿qué le regalamos a mamá por su cumpleaños?
lines.meaning: Raúl, what shall we give Mum for her birthday?
lines.note: le … a mamá: the double is normal

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No sé. ¿Le compramos un libro? Le encanta leer.
lines.meaning: I don't know. Shall we buy her a book? She loves reading.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ya le regalé uno el año pasado. ¿Qué te parece una bufanda?
lines.meaning: I already gave her one last year. What do you think of a scarf?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Me parece bien. ¿Se la compramos en la tienda de la plaza?
lines.meaning: Sounds good to me. Shall we buy it for her at the shop on the square?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí. Pero me faltan veinte euros. ¿Me los prestas?
lines.meaning: Yes. But I'm twenty euros short. Will you lend them to me?
lines.note: faltar · me los: indirect, then direct

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Vale, te los presto, pero me los devuelves el viernes.
lines.meaning: OK, I'll lend them to you, but you give them back to me on Friday.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Te lo prometo. ¿Y a papá? ¿Le decimos algo?
lines.meaning: I promise. And Dad? Shall we tell him anything?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Mejor no le decimos nada. A él le gustan las sorpresas.
lines.meaning: Better not to tell him anything. He likes surprises.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: De acuerdo. Y le pido la tarta a la tía Rosa. Nos la hace siempre.
lines.meaning: Agreed. And I'll ask Aunt Rosa for the cake. She always makes it for us.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Perfecto. Le escribo un mensaje ahora mismo.
lines.meaning: Perfect. I'll write her a message right now.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Qué bien! Solo nos quedan dos días.
lines.meaning: Great! We only have two days left.
lines.note: quedar: verb agrees with dos días

bites.title: To whom? For whom?
bites.rule: The indirect object receives the thing or the action. The pronouns are me, te, le, nos, os, les. Le and les have no gender, so a Juan, a Marta and a usted all take le.
bites.example: Le regalo flores. Te escribo un correo.
bites.example_meaning: I give her flowers. I'll write you an email.

bites.title: Say it twice
bites.rule: Spanish keeps the pronoun even when the person is named: Le regalo flores a mi madre. Add a él / a ella / a usted to make le clear or to stress it.
bites.example: A mí me gusta el café, pero a él le gusta el té.
bites.example_meaning: I like coffee, but he likes tea.

bites.title: Le + lo = se lo
bites.rule: Two pronouns: indirect first, then direct. Le or les before lo / la / los / las turns into se: Le doy el libro becomes Se lo doy.
bites.example: ¿El libro? Se lo doy a Juan.
bites.example_meaning: The book? I'll give it to Juan.

bites.title: Gustar's family
bites.rule: Encantar, interesar, parecer, doler, faltar and quedar work like gustar. You use a pronoun plus the verb, and the verb agrees with the thing: me duele la cabeza, me duelen los pies.

sorts.title: Direct or indirect?
sorts.why: If the person is the one seen, invited or called, the pronoun is direct (lo/la). If something is given, sent or written to them, it is indirect (le/les).

sorts.title: Le or les?
sorts.why: One person (him, her, usted) takes le. Several people (them, ustedes) take les. Gender does not matter.

sorts.title: The verb agrees with the thing
sorts.why: With gustar-type verbs the person is me/te/le and the verb matches the thing. A singular thing takes duele / falta, and a plural thing takes duelen / faltan.

spots.sentence: Lo regalo flores a mi madre.
spots.why: Mi madre receives the flowers, so she is the indirect object and the pronoun is le.

spots.sentence: Le envío una foto a mis padres.
spots.why: Mis padres are plural, so the pronoun is les.
Le turns into se before lo: se lo doy.
Faltar agrees with the thing: un euro is singular, so falta.
Parecer agrees with la película, singular: parece.

spots.sentence: A mis padres le interesa la historia.
spots.why: The pronoun must match a mis padres, so it is the plural les.
